brief: Goldman Sachs European equity sales round-up, not a single argument. SX5E +17bps on low volume with US markets closed for Labour Day, US and Bund 10yr at 4.77% and 3.38%, Brent $98, gold $4435, bitcoin $79k. Canada's retaliatory tariffs on US goods took effect and both sides say they want a deal. Copper made a new high above $14500 on renewed US tariff risk and a tight physical market, so the GS copper mining basket should outperform as demand rises. GS raises Brent forecasts $5 to $85 and $80 for Dec 2026 and 2027, assuming Mideast shipping disruption persists into 2027, and keeps the upgrade modest because OECD commercial inventories have barely drawn since the Iran war began. That war has cost US consumers $100bn, about $760 per household since February. A GS option trader reads S&P six-month realized correlation at 11 as unsustainable and ending in an index vol convexity starburst. GS expects a fully priced 25bp ECB hike Thursday and September as the last of the cycle. Hedge fund net leverage rose but stays in the 4th percentile. Sector stance is overweight Technology, Banks, Defence, Telecoms and Renewables versus underweight Autos, Chemicals, Travel & Leisure and Healthcare.
